question: Your extraction pipeline validates each invoice output with Pydantic, which checks that the line item amounts sum to the extracted total. When the check fails, the retry request sends only the validation error text, for example "line items sum to 1,240 but total is 1,420". The retried outputs often change fields that were already correct, and many outputs still fail the same check. Which changes to the retry step best support model self-correction?

options.text: Replace the specific error text with a general instruction telling the model to review its previous extraction carefully and fix mistakes.
options.reason: Specific validation errors guide the model toward the correction. A generic instruction removes the information that says what failed.

options.text: Stop retrying these invoices and send them to human review, because a failed sum check shows the needed values are absent.
options.reason: Retries are ineffective only when the information is absent from the source. Here the amounts are in the invoice, so a retry with proper feedback can succeed.

options.text: Force the extraction tool with tool_choice on the retry so that schema enforcement prevents the line items and total from disagreeing.
options.reason: Tool use with a schema eliminates syntax errors only. A sum mismatch is a semantic validation error, and schema enforcement cannot prevent it.

options.text: Add the full original invoice to the follow-up request so the model can recheck each amount against the source text.
options.reason: The follow-up request should include the original document. Without the invoice, the model cannot verify which value is wrong, so it guesses and changes correct fields.

options.text: Add the failed extraction to the follow-up request so the model can fix the flagged fields instead of regenerating every value.
options.reason: The follow-up request should include the failed extraction together with the specific errors. This lets the model target the flagged fields rather than redo the whole output.
